overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a cool, marine-influenced day with patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies keeping temperatures suppressed. As of 10:35 ET, the running max is only 64.4°F with a modest warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, though the intraday hour-of-max has already been recorded at 09:49 ET — suggesting the peak may come later in the afternoon as marine layer erodes. The pattern is notably cooler than the broader regional heat event, which is concentrated in desert areas well outside LA proper.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread: HRRR is the warmest at 70.2°F, ECMWF at 68.4°F, and NBM most conservative at 67.0°F — a ~3°F range reflecting uncertainty in marine layer burn-off timing. The current observed running max of 64.4°F is well below all model guidance, consistent with fog and cloud cover still suppressing warming through mid-morning.
max_temp_prediction: The META model (most reliable fused signal) concentrates probability most heavily in the 70-71°F bucket (26.7%) and 74-75°F / 76-77°F buckets (~18% each), suggesting a likely final TMAX in the 69–74°F range. The NWS official forecast of 69°F aligns with the lower end of this distribution, while HRRR's 70.2°F and the META peak around 70-71°F suggest 70°F is a reasonable central estimate. Confidence is moderate — marine layer burn-off timing is the key uncertainty, and the early hour-of-max signal at 09:49 ET could mean the day stalls, but models broadly expect continued afternoon warming toward 68–72°F.
